---
title: "FAQ"
---

## Is ACE cloud-based?

No. ACE works with local `.ace` project files.

## Do wording cues use AI or upload my text?

No. Wording cues run locally in ACE. They use SQLite full-text search to compare the focused sentence with code names and definitions in the open project. They do not use an AI model, cloud service, or external search package.

## Can I use ACE with sensitive data?

ACE does not upload project data automatically, but you still need to follow your ethics approval, data management plan, and institutional storage requirements. Be careful where you save and back up `.ace` files.

## Can multiple coders use the same project?

ACE is designed for small teams, but it does not provide real-time collaborative editing. In most workflows, coders work on separate project files and then compare agreement.

## How does Quick resume work across desktop windows?

ACE keeps the most recently opened project in a per-user history shared by desktop windows, even when they use different local ports. If two windows open projects at once, the last successful open becomes Quick resume. On first use after updating, ACE imports an older browser Quick resume entry only if no shared choice has been made; clearing Quick resume prevents another window from restoring an older entry. If the shared history is unavailable, that window uses its browser history until the shared history is available again.

## Are layout settings shared between desktop windows?

Yes. Sidebar width, source-grid height, coding text size and width, panel and note-drawer state, and codebook cues follow you when another desktop window opens on a different local port. ACE imports an older browser setting only when no shared choice exists. If the shared settings are temporarily unavailable, the current window keeps its browser setting and retries later. An already open window may need a reload to show a setting changed elsewhere.

## Does ACE remember which source I was reading?

Desktop windows share the last viewed source for each project file and coder, even when their local ports differ. A copy of a project starts with its own position. If two windows navigate in the same project, the last saved position is used next time. When the shared store is unavailable, each window uses its own browser position. Older positions saved only against a project ID reset once because ACE cannot tell which copy of that project they belonged to.

## Why do agreement results differ between codes?

Agreement depends on how often a code is used, how clearly it is defined, and how similarly coders apply it. Low agreement is often a prompt to review the code definition and examples.

## Why does ACE say my project needs a newer version?

The project was last used with a newer version of ACE, and this version cannot read it. ACE has not changed the file. Install the latest release from the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/usyd-soles-edu/annotation-coding-environment/releases/latest) and open the project again. Projects from older versions of ACE open normally: ACE updates them automatically. See [Project files](file-format.qmd).

## Can I copy my project while ACE is open?

Close the project or quit ACE first. While ACE is open, recent work can sit in temporary journal files beside the `.ace` file, so a copy taken then may be incomplete. See [Project files](file-format.qmd).

## Where do I report problems?

Report bugs or documentation issues on the [GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/usyd-soles-edu/annotation-coding-environment/issues).
